short.text: The sky appears blue because of a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering, where sunlight is scattered by gas molecules in the atmosphere. These molecules scatter shorter wavelengths of light, like blue and violet, more effectively than longer wavelengths like red and yellow. This scattered blue light is what we see when we look at the sky.

- **Serving recipe:** Abliterated Jarrelscy ARVQ/NVFP4 hybrid of MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL served on 4 DGX Spark nodes (TP4) with 1M-token context, using image v2 and MTP=2 over all three built-in heads.
- **Performance:** 20.4 tok/s single-stream prose and ~530 tok/s prefill (up from 128 tok/s eager), with 38K-token time-to-first-token of 72 s; MTP=2 remains the champion over DFlash.
- **Tool calling:** MiMo tool-call parsers are enabled and Hermes executes tools (`write_file`, `terminal`, `execute_code`), with the infinite tool-loop
